messages:
alex: Hey folks — terraform apply against prod failed, getting a state lock error. Anyone running an apply?

alex: ```
Error: Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed

Lock Info:
  ID: 12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef
  Operation: OperationTypeApply
  Who: alex
  Version: v1.2.3
```

infra-bot: Reminder: S3/DynamoDB state locking enabled. Use `terraform force-unlock` only after confirming no concurrent runs :warning:

riley: I started a deploy earlier but it finished. Could be a stale lock. Alex can you try `terraform force-unlock 12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef` from the runner or locally?

alex: ran `terraform force-unlock 12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef` and got: `Error: No matching lock found`. Lock ID might have rotated. Running `terraform plan` now shows drift too:

alex: ```
  # aws_instance.web will be updated in-place
~ aws_instance.web
    instance_type: "t3.medium" => "t3.large"
```

sam: ok that means someone changed the instance outside TF. Before applying anything, we should import the real resource and refresh state. What's the instance id?

alex: instance id is i-0abcd1234

alex: `terraform state list` -> shows `aws_instance.web`
alex: `terraform state show aws_instance.web` -> instance_type = t3.medium in state

alex: AWS console shows i-0abcd1234 is actually t3.large

riley: import it: `terraform import aws_instance.web i-0abcd1234` then `terraform refresh` and `terraform plan` to be sure.

alex: ran import: 
```
aws_instance.web: Importing from ID "i-0abcd1234"...
aws_instance.web: Import complete!
```

alex: after import + refresh, `terraform plan` still shows a diff: TF config wants t3.medium, actual is t3.large, so plan would change infra to t3.medium if we apply. We don't want that.

morgan: simplest safe path: update TF config (variable or module) to t3.large and then run plan/apply. That way TF will match reality and apply should be a no-op. If we wanted to force recreation instead, use `terraform taint aws_instance.web` then apply.

sam: yep — to update only state without touching infra is risky. Import + update config to match is the right move. Also add a check to run `terraform refresh` before any prod apply to catch drift earlier.

alex: steps I'm taking: 1) update TF var to t3.large in the module, 2) run `terraform plan` in prod workspace, 3) apply (should be a no-op).

riley: also I checked the DynamoDB locks table — there was a leftover item with LockID `9876abcd-...`. I removed it after verifying no runs were active. infra-bot: Note: CI drift job sometimes leaves locks if the runner is killed; we've added a TTL but manual cleanup still happens.

alex: updated TF var, ran `terraform plan` — plan shows no changes now. Running apply...

alex: `Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.` :tada:

sam: nice. Quick follow-ups: 1) add a short runbook section about troubleshooting stale locks (DynamoDB table, `force-unlock`, verifying CI runs), 2) add `terraform refresh` to the prod pre-check pipeline, 3) gate prod applies to prevent parallel runs.

morgan: I'll open a pipeline PR for the semaphore guard and add a DynamoDB check step.

alex: Will open the runbook PR now and link it here. Thanks all :thumbsup:

riley: FYI if you ever want to force a replacement: `terraform taint aws_instance.web` then `terraform apply` — recreates the resource. Use sparingly. :eyes:
